stem.text: The level of a pollutant in a lake is modeled by a differentiable function L of time t, measured in days, whose rate of change is \( L'(t) = 13 e^{- \frac{t}{5}} \) parts per billion per day, for \( 0 \le t \le 15 \). Using a calculator, find \( L'(5) \), showing the setup, and interpret the value in the context of the problem with correct units. Give the value correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: \( L'(5) = 4.782 \), so at time t = 5 days the level of the pollutant is increasing at a rate of 4.782 parts per billion per day.

worked_solution.text: With a calculator, \( L'(5) = 4.782 \) to three decimal places.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the derivative at the instant

worked_solution.text: The value is positive, so at time t = 5 days the level of the pollutant is increasing at a rate of 4.782 parts per billion per day.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the direction of change

options.label: \( L'(5) = 4.782 \), so at time t = 5 days the level of the pollutant is moving with a velocity of 4.782 parts per billion per day.
options.derivation: the rate of change of a non-motion quantity called a velocity
